title: Evaluation of the coordinate-free polynomial
statement: Let $F$ be a real coefficient family on subsets of $[n]$, let $i\in[n]$, let $\Omega$ be a measurable space, let $X_j:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ for each $j\in[n]$, and let $\omega\in\Omega$. The random-input evaluation of the polynomial obtained from $F$ by setting to zero every coefficient indexed by a set containing $i$ equals $\displaystyle\sum_{T\subseteq[n]\setminus\{i\}}F(T)\prod_{j\in T}X_j(\omega)$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a real coefficient family on subsets of $[n]$
$X$ is a family of real-valued functions on $\Omega$
replaced: Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{j\in S}x_j$ be a real multilinear polynomial and fix $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Let $X_j\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be arbitrary functions. For each $\omega\in\Omega$, evaluation of the coordinate-free part of $F$ on $X(\omega)$ equals $\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i\}}a_S\prod_{j\in S}X_j(\omega)$.
